facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of an enlarging, intermittently painful, purplish lump in her left ear canal
cracking and pus-filled sores at the site
a 3.5 × 2.5 cm purplish-red mass in the left external ear canal
irregular, friable surface and bleeding on minimal contact
Contrast-enhanced CT of the mastoids showed a lobulated mass in the cutis and subcutis of the left auricle
extending into the external acoustic canal and into the left parotid space
bilateral level II–IV cervical lymph nodes up to 0.6 cm in diameter
CT angiography demonstrated marked vascularity of the mass
supplied by branches of the left superficial temporal and posterior auricular arteries
Incisional biopsy revealed atypical cells and granulomatous inflammation
a provisional diagnosis of an auricular malignant tumor without a clear histopathological subtype

The patient's presentation of cracking and pus-filled sores, along with granulomatous inflammation on incisional biopsy, suggests an inflammatory condition, which could be granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
